ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Yul Brynner — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: New patient visit for six weeks of hoarseness, with a left upper lobe mass on same-day CT

text.paragraph: New patient visit for six weeks of hoarseness, with a left upper lobe mass on same-day CT [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: His voice has become weak and breathy, and he cannot sing or project on stage. [S]
He wants to get back to performing and to keep working for as long as he can. [S]
He wants people to know what smoking did to him. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Yul Brynner was born Yuliy Borisovich Bryner on July 11, 1920, in Vladivostok, Russia. [D]

He gave varying accounts of his origins, saying at times that he was born on Sakhalin Island, with the year given as 1915 (UPI gives July 11, 1915; another reference gives July 12, 1915, under the name Taidje Kahn). [D]
He first played the King of Siam in The King and I on Broadway in 1951, won the Academy Award for best actor in the 1956 film, and played the role 4,625 times over 34 years. [D]

He smoked heavily for decades: UPI reported that at one time he smoked five packs of cigarettes a day, and Cancer Today reports two to four packs a day from the age of 12 and that he quit in 1971. [D]

In September 1983 he was found to have lung cancer; Cancer Today reports that he had found a lump on his vocal cords and that the tumor was too close to his heart for surgery, and UPI reports that he was treated for lung cancer that month and said he would beat the disease and resume touring. [D]

text.paragraph: 4 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

list.item: Former smoker: about 3 packs a day from age 12 until he quit 12 years ago (roughly 115 pack-years); no tobacco, vaping, or cannabis since; wants other smokers to hear his story [S]
Alcohol: a glass of wine with dinner two or three nights a week (AUDIT-C 2); no other drug use [S]
Stage actor and singer, leading a national touring production with eight performances a week; has paused the tour for the tests and wants to return as soon as he safely can [S]
Married; lives in an apartment in New York and on the road during the tour; a company manager and a long-time dresser help with the travel schedule [S]
No occupational asbestos, radon, or diesel exposure known; no family history of lung cancer known to him [S]

text.paragraph: No medications started by this date.

Positive for the concerns in the history of present illness. Alert, commanding, and precise; wants the facts plainly and in full. Worried but composed; PHQ-9 score 5 with item 9 scored 0; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. No other systems reported as affected in this synthetic episode. [S]

list.item: Left vocal fold paralysis with a breathy, weak voice, most likely from left recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement by disease in the aortopulmonary window: active, confirmed [S]
Left upper lobe mass invading the mediastinum, with enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes, on CT at presentation; suspicious for lung cancer pending tissue diagnosis: active, confirmed [S]
Former smoker: about 3 packs a day from age 12 until he quit 12 years ago, roughly 115 pack-years; no tobacco since: active, confirmed [S]

Thoracic oncology consultation for the tissue diagnosis, stage, biomarker plan, first-line therapy, the place of radiation and a bone-modifying agent, and monitoring. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, lung cancer monograph (2026); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (2026) [S]

Staging and tissue diagnosis: FDG PET-CT, brain MRI with contrast, and endobronchial ultrasound-guided needle aspiration of the highest-stage node, with enough tissue for PD-L1 and comprehensive next-generation sequencing, and plasma cell-free DNA testing in parallel. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, lung cancer monograph (2026); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (2026) [S]

First-line systemic therapy chosen by biomarkers once sequencing excludes an actionable alteration: pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for PD-L1 50 percent or more, with response CT every 6 to 12 weeks; switch to 400 mg every 6 weeks to fit the tour once stable. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, lung cancer monograph (2026); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (2026) [S]

Immune-related adverse event monitoring: TSH and free T4, liver tests, creatinine, glucose, and blood count before each infusion; morning cortisol at baseline and for symptoms; written list of warning symptoms (diarrhea, cough or breathlessness, rash, yellowing, severe fatigue or headache) with a 24-hour oncology telephone line. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, lung cancer monograph (2026); Management of Immune-Related Adverse Events in Patients Treated With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy: ASCO Guideline Update (2021) [S]

Early integrated palliative care alongside cancer treatment, starting within eight weeks of diagnosis, with symptom (ESAS) and distress screening at each visit and advance care planning. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, lung cancer monograph (2026); Integration of Palliative Care Into Standard Oncology Care: American Society of Clinical Oncology Clinical Practice Guideline Update (2017); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Distress Management (2026) [S]

If bone metastases are confirmed: zoledronic acid 4 mg every 12 weeks after a dental examination, with calcium and vitamin D and calcium and creatinine checks before each dose; palliative radiation only if a lesion becomes painful or threatens fracture. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, lung cancer monograph (2026); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (2026) [S]

Voice and work: injection medialization of the left vocal fold, voice therapy with a speech-language pathologist, infusions scheduled on his day off, and a graded return to rehearsal and performance as he chooses. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, lung cancer monograph (2026); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (2026) [S]

Tobacco: confirm abstinence at each visit; no cessation treatment needed; record the smoking history for his care team. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, lung cancer monograph (2026); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (2026) [S]
Referral to thoracic oncology, Leah Morrow, MD, ordered 1983-09-01 [S]
